# Social Trends MCP

> Public social trend collection, PostgreSQL history, REST/WebSocket and stdio MCP tools with evidence-based movement analysis. Default sources require no paid API or AI model.

## Documentation
- [Setup and operation](https://github.com/JienWeng/social-trend-mcp/blob/main/README.md): prerequisites, setup and service commands.
- [Supported endpoints and MCP tools](https://github.com/JienWeng/social-trend-mcp/blob/main/docs/ENDPOINTS.md): methods, arguments, persistence and source coverage.
- [Trend analysis](https://github.com/JienWeng/social-trend-mcp/blob/main/TREND-ANALYSIS.md): evidence rules, verification and limitations.
- [Repairs and validation](https://github.com/JienWeng/social-trend-mcp/blob/main/CURRENT-STATUS.md): source and reliability status.
- [Change summary](https://github.com/JienWeng/social-trend-mcp/blob/main/docs/CHANGES.md): implemented repairs and known boundaries.

## Local interfaces
REST base: http://127.0.0.1:8000. GET /openapi.json is the live schema; GET /docs is interactive documentation. GET /llms.txt serves this guide.
GET /api/v1/platforms and /api/v1/regions enumerate supported choices. Platform IDs: twitter, tiktok, youtube, instagram, douyin.
GET /api/v1/feeds/{platform}?region=global&limit=30 fetches a public feed through the shared 120-second cache without persistence.
GET /api/v1/trends and /api/v1/trends/{platform} read stored snapshots. GET /api/v1/trends/history/{platform} reads history.
GET /api/v1/search/exact?q=... and /api/v1/search/discover?q=... fetch observed feeds without persistence.
POST /api/v1/refresh queues persisted collection and returns 202.
POST /api/v1/analysis/capture/{platform}?region=global fetches and persists; 200 means captured, 202 means another capture is running, 502 means collection failed and its failure snapshot was recorded.
GET /api/v1/analysis/trends?region=global&hours=48&limit=20 reads historical movement signals; optional platform. hours:1–720, limit:1–100.
GET /api/v1/analysis/changes?since=ISO-8601 compares stored samples to a checkpoint within the past 30 days; optional platform, region and limit (1–100 per section). Returns added/removed/changed topics, unchanged counts, evidence and separate sustained momentum. Save generated_at as your next checkpoint. Baseline data must have been fetched and completed at/before since.
GET /api/v1/health reports healthy/degraded in its JSON body.
WebSocket /ws/trends broadcasts committed updates; text ping returns pong. Single-worker operation only.

## MCP
Transport: stdio via ./start-mcp.sh; there is no HTTP MCP endpoint.
Tools: get_trends, get_all_trends, exact_search, search_trends (alias), discover_search, list_regions, capture_trends, analyze_trends, get_changes.
Default fetch/search tools use the running API’s shared source cache and do not save history. MCP_FETCH_MODE=direct explicitly enables standalone fetch/search with a process-local cache.
capture_trends requires platform and optionally region; it persists through the API.
analyze_trends accepts optional platform, region, hours and limit; it reads shared stored history.
get_changes requires since (ISO-8601), optional platform, region and limit; reads checkpoint changes without scraping.
Capture, analysis and change-report tools always require the API at API_BASE_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:8000.

## Interpretation rules
Report source scope, actual region, observation times, missing metrics and coverage failures.
X is a third-party ranking. TikTok is a limited preview; global maps to US. YouTube keyless data is weekly music charts; global maps to US. Instagram is a global public Reels recommendation sample, not a platform-wide trends ranking. Douyin is a China hot list; heat scores are not views.
Search covers observed feeds, not full-platform content. Empty results do not prove platform-wide absence.
A rising candidate needs three independent observations over at least one hour, spaced at least 15 minutes, plus sustained rank improvement or comparable metric growth. Repeated source editions count once.
Use returned evidence and warnings. Confidence is qualitative, not a probability. Added/removed in a checkpoint report describe the sampled feed, not platform-wide creation/disappearance. Two-point changes are not sustained momentum. First appearance in a sample is not proof of a newly emerging topic. Do not claim future virality or exhaustive platform coverage.
AI can interpret these signals; the service does not call a paid LLM or validate predictive accuracy.
Collection defaults: X/Douyin hourly, TikTok/Instagram every six hours, YouTube daily. SCRAPE_INTERVAL_HOURS overrides all; SOURCE_INTERVALS_HOURS JSON overrides specific sources. Retrieval freshness is twice the applicable interval. Identical new source-aware content reuses topic rows while preserving every capture and fetched_at retrieval time; existing historical duplicates remain. Referenced canonical snapshots must not be deleted. Do not create synthetic observations in the service database to simulate history.

## Repository layout
The upstream source is pinned to caicai-yao/social-trends-mcp commit c9f413ad1c8c6b387e8cd1af5f0c709f263ceae2.
setup.sh clones it into ignored upstream/, applies verification/repairs.patch and restores verification/regression-tests/. The patch contains the implementation changes; upstream/ is not a Git submodule.
Use ./verification/run_tests.sh for isolated regression checks. Live verification scripts perform network requests and may persist real captures.
